reasons: Proof mismatch: evidence/claude-fix.json (the only fix-run log present, 26 turns, ~98s) reports the result 'PR #13 — parked, iteration cap (2) already reached before this round; no changes applied ... The owner needs to run state/cli.py set-iterations to reset the count before another round can apply it' — i.e. it claims nothing was written to spec.md/plan.md and the overturn is still pending a reset. But this diff (base main...HEAD) plainly shows spec.md's Flagged concern 2 rewritten to Collection[float], plan.md's Order of work/Risks/Options-not-taken rewritten to match, decisions-b.json item 2 marked overturned, and a fourth test added to the plan — i.e. exactly the changes claude-fix.json says were NOT applied. fix-response.md ('round 4', 'Applied: ... gate/cli.py bump-iteration accepted this round') narrates the successful application that matches the diff, but there is no claude-fix.json (or a second, differently-named one) whose logged result matches that successful round; the one committed run-log for this phase contradicts the artifact it is supposed to account for. Either the committed evidence is stale/wrong (left over from the earlier parked attempt and never overwritten), or these spec.md/plan.md edits were made outside the logged, auditable claude-fix run — either way the delegation prompt's own instruction (compare committed evidence against the diff; the evidence must be literal toolchain/run output, not the author's unverified claim) is not satisfied here, and a person should confirm how these edits were actually produced before this round is trusted.

Minor, pre-existing and not fixed by this round: spec.md's Requirements bullet 3 ('...are not decided by this spec pass...') and the Design section's parameter-type paragraph still describe the parameter-type choice as an open Sequence-vs-Iterable question, never mentioning Collection[float] at all, even though Flagged concerns now shows it decided/overturned. The owner's review comment only asked to update 'the closed concern in spec.md' (not the Design prose), so this is in scope of what was skipped, not what was asked — noted as a nit, not a reason on its own, but it compounds with the proof problem above in making spec.md a less reliable single source of truth than plan.md.
classification_reasons: Spec is not fully tight: Flagged concern 2 is closed with a concrete decision (Collection[float]) and plan.md's Order of work states one exact signature/body, but spec.md's Requirements/Design sections still contain stale 'not decided'/'undecided' language for the same concern, so spec.md alone is not internally consistent even though plan.md is.

This is a contract change (mean's parameter type, part of its public signature) decided in this round — sdlc.yaml's routine test explicitly excludes 'a schema or contract change', so routine is unavailable regardless of blast radius.

Blast radius is small in file count (only changes/0002-.../{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**}; no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py or guardrail file is touched) and no risk_list item applies, but mean is brand-new code with no existing test coverage yet (the tests that will exercise it are written in phase c), so the 'code the existing tests already cover' condition for routine also fails.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome and Open questions against the current spec.md/plan.md/decisions-b.*; the owner's overturn of the panel's Sequence[float] pick to Collection[float] (evidence/decisions-b.md item 2, decisions-b.json's overturned field) is faithfully carried into spec.md's Flagged concern 2 and plan.md's signature, body, Risks and Options-not-taken sections — the substance of the change matches what the review comment asked for.

Spec and plan: compared the review comment ('Update the closed concern in spec.md, the signature in plan.md's design and the test names accordingly') against the diff item by item. spec.md's closed concern: updated. plan.md's signature (mean(values: Collection[float]) -> float, importing Collection from typing): updated. 'Test names' accordingly: rather than a bare rename (none of the three existing planned test names encode a parameter type, so a rename wouldn't have proven anything), the run added a fourth test, test_mean_accepts_non_sequence_collection (a set), and bumped the expected pass count from 8 to 9 in both spec.md Acceptance and plan.md Proof, consistently. Considered this scope creep beyond the literal comment, but it is transparently disclosed in fix-response.md as an interpretation, is consistent with coding-standards rule 4 (no behaviour/contract change ships without a test that would fail if the implementation only handled Sequence, e.g. via indexing), and is confined to planning documents (no test code is written in this design-phase diff) — judged defensible, not a reason to escalate on its own.

Found the stale spec.md prose noted above (Requirements bullet 3, Design section) still framing the parameter type as an open Sequence-vs-Iterable question; judged a nit per REVIEW.md ('style and naming are nits'; it does not change what plan.md tells an implementer to build), but noted since it was left untouched even though the closed concern immediately below it was updated.

Proof: this is the finding above — evidence/claude-fix.json's own logged result contradicts the diff it should describe (says 'no changes applied', diff shows spec.md/plan.md substantially rewritten). Checked run-b.json (only records phase/started_at, no help disambiguating), gate-b.json (records the prior, pre-reset gate check at an earlier head, not this round — expected, since the next gate check runs after this review), and status.yaml (gate.result/reason/at are carried over from before the owner's iteration reset, which is consistent with 'gate section reflects the last completed gate/cli.py check' and not itself a red flag; iterations: 1 and iterations_reset_by: luissiviero are consistent with one accepted round after reset).

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own --stat header and a full read that only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**} are touched; no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py, .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml appears; none of sdlc.yaml's risk_list items applies (no code exists yet to touch them).

Policies: re-read the panel's b-2-advocate.md/b-2-reviewer.md and decisions-b.json/.md; the owner's overturn rationale (Collection[float] matches what sum/len actually need, at no extra cost, still rejecting a generator) matches the devil's advocate's original point and coding-standards rule 2/5/8 as applied by spec.md; no policy skill is silently skipped.

Tests: no test code exists yet in this design-phase diff (correct — phase c writes it); evaluated whether the newly planned test_mean_accepts_non_sequence_collection actually distinguishes Collection[float] from Sequence[float] given Python does not enforce type hints at runtime — concluded it still has real value as a regression guard against a future implementation that assumes Sequence-only operations (indexing/slicing) rather than sum()/len(), so it is not a vacuous test.
